description: Fetch the archived content of a URL at a specific Wayback Machine timestamp, or of the capture a Wayback capture URL such as a replay_url names. Resolves to the nearest available capture when the exact timestamp has no snapshot. Returns the capture as text — an HTML page as readable plain text with its markup stripped, another text type (plain text, JSON, XML, JavaScript) as stored — and the replay URL of the capture Wayback served, for browser access. A capture of a PDF, image, or other non-text file fails as non_text_capture. Long text comes one page at a time: has_more and total_chars say what remains, and char_offset reads further — pass it with the url and timestamp the notice names, so every page comes from the same capture; after an archived redirect that url differs from the one sent. Use ia_find_snapshots first to discover valid timestamps for a URL.

char_offset.description: Character offset (UTF-16 code units) into the capture's text where this page starts. For the next page, pass the previous char_offset plus max_chars with the url and timestamp the previous page's notice names, so the page comes from the same capture; after an archived redirect that url differs from the one sent. An offset at or past total_chars returns empty text.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters this page holds. Defaults to the server-configured maximum (IA_MAX_SNAPSHOT_CHARS, typically 50 000); a larger value is served at that maximum, with a notice.

timestamp.description: Target Wayback timestamp: 1–14 digits — YYYYMMDDHHMMSS or a prefix of it — or an ISO 8601 date or UTC date-time such as "2020-01-01" or "2020-01-01T12:00:00Z". A full 14 digits, such as resolved_timestamp or a timestamp from ia_find_snapshots, reads that capture, or the one Wayback redirects it to; a shorter value names a period and resolves to the capture nearest its end ("2015" can resolve to one from early January 2016); blank reads the timestamp of a Wayback capture URL passed as url, else the latest capture. Example: "20200101120000" for noon on January 1, 2020.

url.description: The URL whose archived content to retrieve. A Wayback capture URL — web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>/<url>, such as a replay_url — reads as the URL it archives at its timestamp; a timestamp naming a different one fails as ambiguous_timestamp.

name: ia_get_snapshot

char_offset.description: Character offset (UTF-16 code units) this page starts at.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_timestamp`: timestamp is not blank, 1–14 digits, or an ISO 8601 date or UTC date-time, or names a month, day, hour, minute, or second no Gregorian date and time has; or url is a Wayback capture URL whose timestamp is not 1–14 digits naming a real date and time (field "url"). `ambiguous_timestamp`: url is a Wayback capture URL and timestamp names a different timestamp than the one the URL carries. `no_snapshot_available`: No capture exists near the requested timestamp for this URL, the capture there is an archived error page — the HTTP 4xx or 5xx the site itself returned when it was captured — or the Wayback Machine refused the replay request with an HTTP 4xx, as it does for a site excluded from the archive; or the replay's redirects reach no readable capture — the target of an archived redirect (a capture of the site's own 3xx) was never archived, is an archived error page, or was refused, or the redirects loop, run past 10, or reach a 3xx with no Location or a Location that is not an http(s) Wayback Machine URL — answered after one attempt; or the closest-capture lookup answered HTTP 403, 410, or 451, the Wayback Machine declining to serve the URL at all. `non_text_capture`: The capture Wayback served is not text — a PDF, image, archive, or other non-text media type — so it holds no text to return. `content_fetch_failed`: The archived page could not be fetched — the Wayback Machine answered HTTP 429, or 408, 425, or 5xx after retries, did not answer within the request timeout, or could not be reached, or refused the unmodified (id_) form of a text capture it had replayed, or that form's redirects reached no readable capture — or its nearest capture could not be looked up: the closest-capture lookup found no capture or answered HTTP 429, or 408, 425, or 5xx after retries, an unreadable response, or an error in place of a capture, and its CDX fallback failed or had no time left; or the lookup refused the request with another 4xx, did not answer within the request timeout, or could not be reached; or the lookup and the fetch together did not finish within the call's 55 s deadline (the request timeout when that is longer). Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

has_more.description: True when the capture's text continues past this page; the notice names the url, char_offset, and timestamp that read the next one.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters this page could hold — the requested max_chars, or the server maximum when the request omitted it or asked for more.

notice.description: Set when the replay passed through an archived redirect (a capture of the site's own 3xx) — the capture requested is one, or Wayback first redirected the requested timestamp to a nearest capture that is one — naming each archived redirect's capture timestamp, HTTP status, and target, the text then coming from the capture Wayback served for the last target; when the capture is longer than the 4 MiB read limit (the text comes from its first bytes only); when max_chars is above the server maximum; or when more text follows this page — naming the url, char_offset, and timestamp that read the next one.

replay_url.description: Wayback Machine replay URL (https://web.archive.org) of the capture the text came from — where the replay's redirects ended: Wayback's own to the nearest capture, and archived redirects (a capture of the site's own 3xx, which the notice names), followed for up to 10 redirects on the Wayback Machine.

resolved_status.description: HTTP status Wayback replayed the capture the text came from with — the same capture as resolved_timestamp and replay_url.

resolved_timestamp.description: Timestamp (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) of the capture the text came from, read from replay_url.

text.description: One page of the capture's text: up to max_chars characters from char_offset. An HTML page is reduced to readable plain text: scripts, styles, comments, and tags removed, character references decoded, whitespace collapsed. Another text type (plain text, JSON, XML, JavaScript) is the body as archived, line breaks and markup kept. Taken from at most the first 4 MiB of the capture; a notice says so when it is longer.

total_chars.description: Length of the capture's whole text in characters (UTF-16 code units), counted over the same first 4 MiB the text comes from.

title: Get Wayback Machine Snapshot Content
